universal_research_rules: Detect a change before searching for a stock.
Write the causal chain from external change to earnings and expectations.
Separate fact, interpretation, estimate, and unknown.
Classify demand quality; do not equate pipeline with contracted demand.
Model supply response and scarcity duration.
Establish what is priced in before declaring a thesis variant.
Use industry-specific valuation and accounting checks.

fields.economic_engine: Oilfield activity × service intensity × day/rental rates; economics hinge on upstream capex and equipment utilization.
fields.core_kpis: Rig count; frac spreads; utilization; day rates; backlog/book-to-bill; service pricing; offshore awards; FCF conversion.
fields.leading_indicators: E&P capex budgets; oil/gas strip; tender activity; rig reactivations; equipment lead times.
fields.typical_moats: Technical know-how, installed fleet, high-spec equipment scarcity, customer qualification, local service network.
fields.capital_cycle_supply_response: Very cyclical. High returns trigger fleet/equipment additions; offshore/high-spec assets can have multi-year supply lags.
fields.valuation_lenses: EV/EBITDA, EV/FCF, replacement value, mid-cycle earnings.
fields.accounting_data_traps: Capitalized equipment costs, maintenance vs growth capex, contract backlog quality, asset impairments.
fields.common_failure_modes: Overbuilding capacity, commodity collapse, customer concentration, technological substitution, leverage.
fields.ideal_compounder_setup: Asset-light service niches with recurring consumables/software, high switching costs, disciplined capital allocation.
fields.ideal_inflection_setup: Utilization crosses threshold → pricing rises → incremental margins surge; offshore tender cycle turns.
fields.highest_evi_question: What utilization level historically unlocks pricing? How fast can idle/competing capacity return?

fields.economics: Land rigs earn day rates on contracted working days; offshore rigs have longer mobilization and contracting cycles. Separate owned rigs, labor, reimbursables, idle assets and performance bonuses.
fields.advantage_test: Efficient crews and scarce high-specification rigs can protect returns; stacked rigs are latent competing supply. A long backlog is useful only after termination clauses, customer quality and reactivation cost.
fields.monitoring: Weekly rig counts and tenders; quarterly utilization, day rates, backlog conversion and idle cash burn. Watch renewal pricing rather than average fleet rates alone.
fields.cash_and_accounting: Deduct maintenance, surveys and reactivation investment. EBITDA can rise while debt service and recommissioning consume cash; depreciated book value is not replacement economics.
fields.opportunity_and_falsifier: Inflection: better-priced renewals reach cash before meaningful new capacity returns. Falsifier: customers defer wells or reactivated supply destroys pricing.
fields.next_investigation: Compare HP land-fleet renewal economics with RIG offshore backlog, calculating contract-level cash after activation and the liquidity required before first revenue.
fields.valuation_lens: Model realized volume times netback less operating cost, sustaining investment, taxes and financing. For transport, use contracted volumes, tariff/spread and maintenance. Value reserves or assets under multiple commodity decks, with terminal depletion and full common-equity claims.

fields.economics: Equipment sales, consumable replenishment, completion services and compression rentals have different revenue recurrence. Link customer activity to equipment installed, utilization and aftermarket spend.
fields.advantage_test: Qualification, reliability and field service density can support pricing; commoditized labor and pumping face rapid supply response. Compression requires a separate fleet-return model.
fields.monitoring: Weekly drilling/completion activity; quarterly equipment orders, rental utilization, service pricing, customer capex and aftermarket mix. Check foreign versus domestic spending separately.
fields.cash_and_accounting: Separate growth fleet capex from maintenance, finance leases and working capital. Rental gross margin excludes the cost of owning equipment; acquisition growth needs all consideration.
fields.opportunity_and_falsifier: Compounder: proprietary equipment with recurring replacement demand. Inflection: utilization and pricing recover without equivalent fleet spending. Falsifier: throughput growth does not improve cash per share.
fields.next_investigation: For WHD and AROC, reconstruct new-unit return, renewal duration and maintenance assumptions; compare with a larger diversified service provider through a weaker activity case.

fields.economic_engine: Commodity price × production/refining/storage volumes − lifting/feedstock/capex; midstream adds fee-based throughput.
fields.core_kpis: Production; realized prices; breakeven; decline rate; reserves; crack spreads; throughput; inventories; FCF/bbl; leverage.
fields.leading_indicators: Futures curves; inventories; OPEC/supply policy; rig activity; refinery outages; pipeline flows; LNG capacity.
fields.typical_moats: Low-cost resource, advantaged acreage, scale, integrated assets, pipeline rights-of-way, long-term contracts.
fields.capital_cycle_supply_response: Upstream/mining highly cyclical; pipelines slower; refinery capacity additions take years but utilization can swing quickly.
fields.valuation_lenses: NAV, EV/EBITDA, FCF yield, EV/boe/d, P/NAV; DCF for contracted midstream.
fields.accounting_data_traps: Reserve estimates, hedging, asset retirement obligations, maintenance capex, working-capital swings, MLP adjustments.
fields.common_failure_modes: Commodity mean reversion, depletion, political/regulatory risk, leverage, poor acquisitions, stranded assets.
fields.ideal_compounder_setup: Low-cost reserves or fee-based infrastructure with disciplined reinvestment and per-share capital returns.
fields.ideal_inflection_setup: Supply deficit, refinery bottleneck, gas/LNG basis change, capex discipline creates FCF step-up.
fields.highest_evi_question: What marginal supply sets price, and what capex is required to sustain—not grow—production?

fields.economics: Upstream production, refining, chemicals and marketing provide partly offsetting exposures. Segment transfer prices and regional tax regimes affect where profit appears.
fields.advantage_test: Low-cost resources, integration and logistics improve resilience; capital scale does not guarantee project discipline. Frontier developments can lock up capital for a decade.
fields.monitoring: Monthly oil/gas balances and refining spreads; quarterly segment production, realized prices, outages, project milestones and organic reserve replacement.
fields.cash_and_accounting: Value each segment using compatible commodity assumptions. Deduct sustaining and abandonment spending, minority claims, pensions and project commitments; do not net all cash against all project debt.
fields.opportunity_and_falsifier: Inflection: advantaged projects enter production as spending peaks. Falsifier: cost escalation or weak downstream spreads absorb upstream gains.
fields.next_investigation: Build a segment sum-of-parts and five-year sources/uses schedule for XOM versus CVX with flat commodity prices; identify which projects improve cash per diluted share.

fields.economics: Owned working interests receive production cash and fund wells; royalties receive a share of production with limited drilling expense. Split oil, gas and NGL realizations and owned versus noncontrolling economics.
fields.advantage_test: Advantaged acreage, low operating cost and superior development timing matter. Royalty rights can outlive wells, but producing cash declines without new development.
fields.monitoring: Weekly storage/prices; quarterly production, base decline, lateral productivity, hedges, operator activity and reserve replacement. Gas-equivalent volumes are not equivalent revenue.
fields.cash_and_accounting: Use asset NAV and cash under a neutral commodity deck. Include sustaining wells, acquired acreage, abandonment, hedges, preferred claims and dilution; royalty acquisitions are real reinvestment.
fields.opportunity_and_falsifier: Compounder candidate: disciplined low-cost or royalty allocation. Inflection: infrastructure unlocks profitable production. Falsifier: weaker well quality or per-share dilution offsets headline growth.
fields.next_investigation: Extend the VNOM/BSM work into a five-year decline/development bridge; compare with EOG's fully funded production cash using the same prices and tax assumptions.

fields.economics: Refiners earn product values less crude, energy and operating costs; retailers/distributors earn local fuel and merchandise margins. Renewable fuels have feedstock, credit and policy economics distinct from crude refining.
fields.advantage_test: Complex plants, location and logistics can protect differentials; utilization and outages determine short-run scarcity. High benchmark crack spreads may not match an issuer's actual product slate.
fields.monitoring: Weekly product inventories, runs and regional cracks; quarterly capture rates, turnaround schedule, renewable feedstock/credit economics and retail gallons.
fields.cash_and_accounting: Normalize turnaround cash and inventory effects. Renewable credits and environmental liabilities can overwhelm segment EBITDA; separate pipeline subsidiaries and their outside owners.
fields.opportunity_and_falsifier: Inflection: regional product tightness overlaps reliable capacity. Falsifier: imports, new capacity or weak crack capture prevent cash realization.
fields.next_investigation: For VLO versus MPC, bridge a published crack to actual realized margin, scheduled downtime, maintenance and shareholder cash; stress credit-dependent renewable profits separately.

fields.economics: Pipelines, terminals and LNG facilities earn capacity/throughput fees and sometimes commodity-linked margins. A reservation payment, minimum-volume commitment and take-or-pay contract transfer different risks.
fields.advantage_test: Rights-of-way, network connectivity and permitted locations are scarce. New projects can still be overbuilt or dependent on one basin, shipper or export destination.
fields.monitoring: Monthly flows, storage, LNG feedgas and permits; quarterly recontracting spreads, utilization, counterparty credit and project cost-to-complete.
fields.cash_and_accounting: Reconcile distributable cash with maintenance and expansion capex, equity interests, debt guarantees and project financing. Contract duration must not be modeled as perpetuity.
fields.opportunity_and_falsifier: Compounder: connected networks with high incremental returns. Inflection: funded projects enter service. Falsifier: contracted revenue is offset by overruns, weak shippers or renewal compression.
fields.next_investigation: Compare EPD fee cash with LNG's contracted and merchant exposure; calculate distributable cash after the entire committed build and debt maturities, not only this year's capex.

fields.economics: Thermal coal, metallurgical coal and nuclear fuel have different customers and cycles. Uranium contract pricing, conversion and enrichment cannot be modeled using coal tonnage economics.
fields.advantage_test: Resource quality, transport access and permits can constrain supply; long contracts can protect or delay exposure to rising prices. Environmental closure obligations persist after revenue ends.
fields.monitoring: Monthly utility fuel demand and commodity inventories; quarterly contracted/unpriced sales, mine development, realized prices and nuclear-fuel contracting.
fields.cash_and_accounting: Deduct reclamation, sustaining mines and committed production purchases. Reserve duration and contract floors matter more than a peak dividend; distinguish commodity inventory from excess cash.
fields.opportunity_and_falsifier: Inflection: contract resets or restart economics improve realized cash. Falsifier: contracted purchases cost more than deliveries earn, or closure liabilities consume the apparent surplus.
fields.next_investigation: Build separate CCJ contracting and coal cash models, with no shared valuation multiple; check whether price upside belongs to future uncommitted volume or has already been sold.

fields.economic_engine: Price × volume − feedstock/energy; mix ranges from commodity plants to high-value formulations.
fields.core_kpis: Price/mix; volumes; utilization; feedstock spreads; inventories; EBITDA/ton; working capital; ROIC.
fields.leading_indicators: Distributor inventories; plant operating rates; ethane/naphtha spreads; customer production; capacity shutdowns.
fields.typical_moats: Process know-how, formulation IP, qualification, switching costs, scale, feedstock advantage.
fields.capital_cycle_supply_response: Commodity chemicals respond via plant additions/closures; specialty capacity often less fungible and slower to qualify.
fields.valuation_lenses: EV/EBITDA, normalized FCF, P/E, replacement cost; specialty names may warrant ROIC-based DCF.
fields.accounting_data_traps: Inventory gains/losses, restructuring add-backs, environmental liabilities, pension costs, maintenance capex.
fields.common_failure_modes: Capacity glut, feedstock disadvantage, customer destocking, China supply, environmental liabilities.
fields.ideal_compounder_setup: Specialty portfolio with specification lock-in, recurring formulations, pricing power and low capital intensity.
fields.ideal_inflection_setup: Destocking ends → utilization/pricing recover; feedstock spread widens; competitor capacity exits.
fields.highest_evi_question: Is the product truly differentiated or merely marketed as specialty?

fields.economics: Commodity chemical plants earn product/feedstock spreads across operating capacity. Ethylene, polyethylene, PVC and chlor-alkali have different co-product and demand balances.
fields.advantage_test: Low-cost feedstocks and integrated plants matter; announced and idled global capacity set the supply response. A temporary outage is not structural pricing power.
fields.monitoring: Monthly regional spreads, energy, imports and plant starts; quarterly utilization, inventory and sales volumes. Follow Chinese export capacity and construction/consumer demand separately.
fields.cash_and_accounting: Account for turnarounds, environmental obligations, inventory valuation and joint ventures. At the trough a high P/E may be less informative than liquidity and normalized spread earnings.
fields.opportunity_and_falsifier: Inflection: closures and restocking lift sustainable utilization. Falsifier: new export supply caps margins despite local demand recovery.
fields.next_investigation: Choose one chain, such as PVC, and compare regional cash costs and utilization for WLK versus integrated peers; require demand-led operating cash beyond inventory release.
fields.valuation_lens: Use midcycle free cash and asset returns after sustaining and environmental investment. Test price-cost lags, energy intensity, utilization and working capital. For finite resources use reserve/depletion value; for qualified specialty products test incremental returns and customer retention.

fields.economics: Diversified chemical groups combine commodity chains, specialties and sometimes agriculture. Consolidated margins can hide fundamentally different price mechanisms and capital needs.
fields.advantage_test: Integration can reduce costs but complicate accountability. Portfolio simplification creates value only if proceeds, stranded overhead and lost integration benefits reconcile.
fields.monitoring: Quarterly segment volumes, price-cost, utilization, restructuring, divestiture terms and central expenses; monthly downstream production and energy inputs.
fields.cash_and_accounting: Use segment-specific normalized earnings and allocated capital. Include restructuring cash, pensions, environmental liabilities and minority interests; avoid a blanket conglomerate discount assumption.
fields.opportunity_and_falsifier: Inflection: operational repair and divestiture cash improve return on retained capital. Falsifier: recurring restructuring merely resets adjusted earnings.
fields.next_investigation: Study BASF by chain and geography, then compare the retained company's cash after transformation costs with what a simple segment sum-of-parts implies.

fields.economics: Nitrogen depends heavily on gas costs; potash/phosphate on resource and processing economics; crop protection on farmer adoption, channel inventory and product protection.
fields.advantage_test: Cost-advantaged feedstock and deposits protect fertilizer margins; patented molecules and distribution support crop protection. Farmer affordability limits pricing across both.
fields.monitoring: Monthly crop prices, fertilizer costs, acreage and export flows; quarterly channel inventories, application volumes, natural-gas exposure and new-product mix.
fields.cash_and_accounting: Separate dealer destocking from farmer consumption; capitalize no speculative nutrient peak. Include mine life, environmental spending, receivables seasonality and product-development economics.
fields.opportunity_and_falsifier: Inflection: inventory normalization at unchanged farm demand or favorable global cost curves. Falsifier: weak farm income delays applications and increases credit risk.
fields.next_investigation: Compare CF nitrogen cash at several gas-price locations with FMC consumption/channel data; do not infer a common agricultural recovery from their reported sales.

fields.economics: On-site plants earn long-term contracted returns, merchant bulk gas depends on distribution density, and packaged gases depend on local service. Hydrogen megaprojects introduce different demand risk.
fields.advantage_test: Switching an on-site supplier is disruptive and local density helps delivered cost. Attractive legacy contracts do not establish the return of a new speculative plant.
fields.monitoring: Quarterly project backlog conversion, contractual pass-through, same-site volume, price and cost-to-complete. Track customer credit and take-or-pay strength before construction.
fields.cash_and_accounting: Measure after-tax project IRR including ramp losses, maintenance and energy. Backlog is not equity value; committed megaprojects can exceed near-term free cash.
fields.opportunity_and_falsifier: Compounder: contracted projects with proven demand and disciplined capital. Falsifier: weak offtake, delayed commissioning or cost inflation turns growth into financing pressure.
fields.next_investigation: Compare LIN's project-return discipline with APD project commitments, matching each material build to offtake, energy inputs, funding and downside cash needs.

fields.economics: Specialty additives, coatings and formulated materials earn value from performance in a customer's process. End-market volumes and input pass-through still affect reported growth.
fields.advantage_test: Qualification, application expertise and low customer cost relative to failure can protect pricing. Formula ownership alone is not a moat if competing products are easy to approve.
fields.monitoring: Quarterly organic volume, pricing, raw-material lag and new-customer wins; monthly auto, construction and industrial activity. Compare sell-through with distributor restocking.
fields.cash_and_accounting: Normalize restructuring and acquisition adjustments, environmental liabilities and inventory costs. Capitalize only demonstrated recurring gross profit after R&D and commercial support.
fields.opportunity_and_falsifier: Compounder: repeat qualified applications. Inflection: volume recovery after inputs/prices reset. Falsifier: margin recovery depends only on falling inputs while customer volumes deteriorate.
fields.next_investigation: For IOSP versus coatings peers, reconstruct unit volume and price-cost by application, then estimate incremental cash from recovered utilization after working-capital rebuild.

fields.economic_engine: Local price × volume − quarry/cement/aggregate production and freight costs; geography matters enormously.
fields.core_kpis: Tons/shipments; price/ton; aggregates margins; cement utilization; backlog; public/private construction mix.
fields.leading_indicators: Infrastructure awards; housing starts; nonres construction; DOT budgets; cement imports; weather.
fields.typical_moats: Permits/reserves, local scarcity, transportation economics, route density, vertical integration.
fields.capital_cycle_supply_response: New quarries/cement plants face permitting and long lead times; local shortages can persist for years.
fields.valuation_lenses: EV/EBITDA, FCF, value per reserve ton, replacement value.
fields.accounting_data_traps: Depletion, reclamation liabilities, acquisition accounting, weather normalization, land values.
fields.common_failure_modes: Construction downturn, overpaying for reserves, energy inflation, permitting changes.
fields.ideal_compounder_setup: Local oligopoly with scarce permitted reserves and consistent price > cost inflation.
fields.ideal_inflection_setup: Volume trough + continued price increases; infrastructure spend hits constrained local supply.
fields.highest_evi_question: How many years of permitted reserves exist, and can competitors economically truck material into the market?

fields.economics: Aggregates earn local delivered spreads; cement requires kiln utilization and energy; lime is specification/customer driven; wallboard is more housing-sensitive. These are distinct economic submodels.
fields.advantage_test: Permits, reserve location and freight costs limit the economical shipping radius. A local supply constraint does not automatically protect every product sold by the same group.
fields.monitoring: Monthly construction starts and spending; quarterly tons, net pricing excluding freight, cash costs, weather and backlog by geography.
fields.cash_and_accounting: Deduct quarry development, stripping, kiln maintenance and expansion capex. Land reserves do not eliminate replacement investment; freight pass-through must not inflate economic growth.
fields.opportunity_and_falsifier: Compounder: scarce local resources with disciplined capacity. Inflection: utilization recovers into limited supply. Falsifier: costs absorb price or a new kiln earns below its capital cost.
fields.next_investigation: Use the prior USLM/VMC work to model location-specific price-cost and the incremental operating profit needed for each expansion to clear an after-tax return hurdle.

fields.economic_engine: Units × price/mix − resin/metal/fiber and conversion cost; demand tied to consumer/industrial volumes.
fields.core_kpis: Volumes; price-cost spread; resin/paper/aluminum inputs; utilization; contract resets; EBITDA/ton/unit.
fields.leading_indicators: Packaging volumes; retailer inventories; resin/pulp prices; capacity closures; customer contract renewals.
fields.typical_moats: Scale, customer integration, efficient plants, local freight advantage; usually modest differentiation.
fields.capital_cycle_supply_response: Cyclical and prone to overcapacity; closures/consolidation can restore pricing.
fields.valuation_lenses: EV/EBITDA, FCF yield, normalized margins.
fields.accounting_data_traps: Pass-through timing, restructuring charges, pension, lease obligations, maintenance capex.
fields.common_failure_modes: Overcapacity, customer bargaining power, input spikes, secular packaging substitution.
fields.ideal_compounder_setup: Niche packaging with high switching costs, specialized formats, disciplined consolidation.
fields.ideal_inflection_setup: Capacity closures + demand stabilization → price-cost spread expansion.
fields.highest_evi_question: Are price increases contractual pass-throughs or genuine pricing power?

fields.economics: Metal cans, glass and rigid plastic packaging supply consumer units through large production networks. Container volume and customer beverage/food demand matter more than raw-material-inflated sales.
fields.advantage_test: Qualification, plant proximity and efficient production can create advantage; capacity additions and customer bargaining can erode it. Glass furnaces and can lines have different maintenance cycles.
fields.monitoring: Quarterly units, utilization, beverage/customer volumes, input-price resets and new lines; monthly consumption and inventory signals.
fields.cash_and_accounting: Separate metal pass-through from conversion margin. Include furnace rebuilds, restructuring cash, leases and customer-funded assets; EBITDA before maintenance overstates owner cash.
fields.opportunity_and_falsifier: Inflection: utilization improves after industry capacity discipline. Falsifier: overcapacity or customer destocking offsets mix gains.
fields.next_investigation: Compare BALL/CCK can economics with OI glass using cash per unit and sustaining capital; test whether an earnings rebound survives normal energy and rebuild spending.

fields.economics: Corrugated, paperboard and flexible packaging convert fiber/resin into customer protection and display. Integrated mills earn commodity spreads as well as conversion margins.
fields.advantage_test: Mill cost position, recycling access, customer qualification and local converting density matter. Capacity closures can help pricing but lost volume can strand fixed costs.
fields.monitoring: Monthly box shipments, inventories and published prices; quarterly actual price realization, consumer/industrial volume, downtime and acquisition integration.
fields.cash_and_accounting: Reconcile cash perimeter, receivables sales, capex, input lags, disposal proceeds and debt/hedge settlement. Published price increases are not collected cash.
fields.opportunity_and_falsifier: Inflection: price realization and mill utilization improve after portfolio repair. Falsifier: financing or inventory release explains most apparent cash recovery.

fields.economic_engine: Commodity price × volume − cash cost − sustaining/growth capex; ore grade and mine life dominate.

fields.economics: Aluminum spans bauxite, alumina, primary smelting and fabrication. Benchmark metal, regional premiums and power costs create different margins at each stage.

fields.cash_and_accounting: Rate-base growth is not free cash flow; include debt and equity funding, construction interest, pension costs and disallowed spending. Fuel pass-through can inflate revenue without improving profit.

governing_methodology.name: Causal long-term per-share compounding
governing_methodology.objective: Prioritize durable growth in intrinsic value per diluted share by reasoning from external structural change into future industry and company economics.

thesis_construction_order.question: What durable external change is occurring, why is it happening, and over what horizon?
How does the change alter demand, supply, cost curves, bargaining power, regulation, capital intensity, competitive structure, or the location of the profit pool?
Why is this company positioned to benefit, and why should its advantage survive competition, substitution, and supply response?
Through what mechanism does the advantage become retained revenue, margins, cash flow, or lower risk, and how much value remains after stakeholder responses?
Where can the company redeploy capital, at what incremental return, with what funding requirement, and for how long before returns decay?
What can owner earnings, free cash flow, and intrinsic value per diluted share compound to after necessary reinvestment, dilution, debt, acquisitions, dividends, and repurchases?
Which dated filings, operating data, cash reconciliations, and counter-evidence support or break each prior link, and what observation would force the thesis to change?
What expectations are embedded in price, what return and downside follow from the causal scenarios, and what margin of safety remains?

operating_rules.outside_in_reasoning: Reason from external structural changes, including technology and cost curves, regulation, demographics, geopolitics, customer behavior, and industry capacity, into future industry structure and company economics.
operating_rules.evidence_timing: Evidence must test every link continuously; the financial evidence/falsification stage is the formal audit, not permission to postpone verification.
operating_rules.numbers_policy: Numbers are evidence and checkpoints, not the thesis itself.
operating_rules.forecast_rule: Forecasts must be outputs of causal reasoning. If evidence contradicts a necessary link, revise or reject the thesis rather than forcing the model to preserve it.
operating_rules.short_term_inflections: Preserve the separate shorter-term inflection mandate and apply the same causal discipline on its shorter horizon.

anti_patterns.warning: Do not use this sequence as the primary idea-generation or underwriting process.
anti_patterns.reason: It can create false precision without explaining why the KPI should grow, who captures the value, why the economics persist, what capital is required, or whether value compounds per share.
anti_patterns.permitted_downstream_use: KPIs, EPS forecasts, scenarios, and target prices remain useful as tests, measurement, falsification, expectations analysis, and valuation after the causal thesis is explicit.

cross_industry_relationships.mechanism: Mortgage rates and credit → transactions/starts → building products, appliances, furniture, moving/storage and brokerage
cross_industry_relationships.monitor: Track permits, starts, completions and financing separately; completions create apartment supply while transactions stimulate repair and moving demand.
cross_industry_relationships.failure_of_inference: Builder incentives can support new-home sales while existing-home turnover remains weak. Do not infer one broad housing recovery from a single series.

cross_industry_relationships.mechanism: Funded compute demand → energized data centers → networks/chips/equipment → generation and grid investment
cross_industry_relationships.monitor: Match signed customer commitments, grid rights, construction, equipment delivery and in-service dates. Track gross profit and funded returns at each supplier.
cross_industry_relationships.failure_of_inference: A megawatt may appear in several announcements. Avoid counting the same project as independent demand and capitalizing everyone at scarcity margins.

cross_industry_relationships.mechanism: Commodity balances → producer budgets → drilling/services → transport/storage → refining and petrochemical spreads
cross_industry_relationships.monitor: Watch actual producer cash budgets and decline replacement, not only spot prices; compare regional basis, refinery utilization and chemical feedstock spreads.
cross_industry_relationships.failure_of_inference: Higher oil can help producers while hurting consumer demand or chemical margins. Contracted transport revenue may lag and retain counterparty risk.

cross_industry_relationships.mechanism: Weather/crop balances → fertilizer and farm equipment → processing/ingredients → packaged food → distributors/retailers
cross_industry_relationships.monitor: Track crop economics, local basis, inventory, realized pricing and consumer volume; identify contract reset lags and where branded value is retained.
cross_industry_relationships.failure_of_inference: Falling inputs can first reduce processors' revenue or inventory value before helping branded margins. Consumer trade-down can benefit one channel and hurt another.

cross_industry_relationships.mechanism: End-user orders → distributor inventory → component/plant production → freight and warehousing
cross_industry_relationships.monitor: Align sell-in, sell-through, shipments and inventories by calendar. Require orders plus actual use plus cash conversion before calling a broad recovery.
cross_industry_relationships.failure_of_inference: Restocking can lift manufacturers ahead of final demand; heavier freight mix or fuel surcharge revenue can mimic unit growth.

cross_industry_relationships.mechanism: Payer pricing/utilization → provider staffing and collections → equipment/supplies/drugs → property operator coverage
cross_industry_relationships.monitor: Map who bears claims risk, who bills, who gets paid and on what lag; compare reimbursement growth with labor, acuity and denial costs.
cross_industry_relationships.failure_of_inference: Higher utilization may help suppliers/providers but hurt insurers. More covered lives need not create equivalent recognized revenue or landlord rent coverage.

cross_industry_relationships.mechanism: Lending standards/rates → borrower liquidity → defaults and collateral values → bank/insurer/REIT capital
cross_industry_relationships.monitor: Build maturity and funding ladders, then test operating cash and collateral values together. Watch covenant headroom and required capital, not just interest coverage.
cross_industry_relationships.failure_of_inference: Lower rates can relieve borrowers while compressing investment spreads or accelerating mortgage prepayments. Asset and liability duration must be matched.

cross_industry_relationships.mechanism: Engagement/intent → advertising budgets → platforms/agencies/publishers → commerce conversion
cross_industry_relationships.monitor: Track advertiser outcomes, retained take rates, user retention and content costs. Distinguish distribution access from owning the customer relationship.
cross_industry_relationships.failure_of_inference: Audience growth may not monetize; automated content can lower production cost while reducing scarcity and pricing for creators and intermediaries.

cross_industry_relationships.mechanism: Hiring/wage pressure → staffing and outsourced services → software/equipment substitution → customer productivity
cross_industry_relationships.monitor: Compare worker output, service quality and customer savings. Test whether suppliers retain productivity gains or pass them through in lower prices.
cross_industry_relationships.failure_of_inference: A falling wage bill can signal lost volume or poor staffing rather than durable efficiency. AI spending alone does not prove customer returns.

cross_industry_relationships.mechanism: Claims inflation/catastrophes → insurance pricing → broker commissions → customer expenses/property cash
cross_industry_relationships.monitor: Compare rate with exposure and loss trend; trace premium increases into broker revenue and insured-property expense. Check reinsurance terms and retained catastrophe risk.
cross_industry_relationships.failure_of_inference: An insurer's favorable investment income does not fix inadequate reserves; rising premiums can raise broker revenue while weakening customers' occupancy or operating margins.

cross_industry_relationships.mechanism: End-use technology → metal/mineral mix → extraction/processing → equipment and infrastructure
cross_industry_relationships.monitor: Map physical content, recovery/recycling, qualification and supply additions. Compare substitution economics at several prices rather than extrapolating current scarcity.
cross_industry_relationships.failure_of_inference: A long-run demand narrative can coexist with near-term oversupply, higher extraction costs and shareholder dilution.

cross_industry_relationships.mechanism: Customer contracts → working capital/construction → revenue recognition → cash collection → shareholder cash
cross_industry_relationships.monitor: Record contract enforceability, termination terms, milestone timing, funding source and diluted shares. Match business perimeter across statements.
cross_industry_relationships.failure_of_inference: Backlog, rate authorization, eligible lives, leased megawatts and acquisition accretion all precede cash. None independently proves funded per-share value creation.
